prompt: Create ONE single image, 4:3 aspect ratio: a 2x2 grid of 4 SEPARATE illustrations (2 columns, 2 rows) for a children's picture book, all panels exactly the same size and perfectly aligned, plain white gutters between and around the panels, no frames, no captions, no text, letters or numbers anywhere. Style: Children's picture-book illustration, soft watercolor and gouache with gentle pencil lines, warm golden light, earthy palette (stone beige, olive green, terracotta, deep blue), rounded friendly faces with expressive eyes, the Land of Israel and Babylon in the time of the Mishnah and Talmud (Roman era): stone houses with flat roofs, oil lamps, study halls with low benches and scrolls, markets, olive and carob trees. Jewish sages with beards, tunics and simple robes; women in modest long dresses and head coverings. Calm, warm, safe mood. HEAD COVERING RULE for every panel: every man and every boy (including sons, shepherds, servants, neighbors and children) ALWAYS has his head covered, never bare: a kippah (skullcap) in modern or sages-era scenes, a tallit worn over the head, or in ancient scenes the hood or corner of his robe/cloak drawn over his head or a head-cloth tied with a cord. This overrides any mention of hair in a character description (the hair may show beneath the covering). Women and girls keep their head scarves or coverings as described. Keep every character exactly the same in every panel where they appear: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa: humble sage about 50, thin build, olive skin, long soft grey-brown beard, gentle smiling dark eyes with laugh lines, plain off-white head wrap; very simple patched light-brown wool robe over a cream tunic with tzitzit corners, rope belt, bare feet or simple sandals; Chanina's daughter: girl about 9, slim, olive skin, big dark eyes, long dark braid under a light rose-pink head scarf, long modest soft-yellow dress with long sleeves and a small cream apron; The lamp: a small round terracotta Shabbat oil lamp with a short spout and a single bright, cheerful golden flame, standing on a simple wooden shelf. Panels in reading order: 1 BOOK COVER: In a tiny clean stone home at dusk, Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa and his daughter sit side by side, gazing with joy at the small terracotta lamp whose golden flame burns bright and steady, lighting their faces. He has an arm around her shoulders. Two simple clay jars stand on the shelf nearby. Warm glowing light against deep blue twilight in the window. Intimate composition, the flame at the center. 2 Friday afternoon. A tiny, very plain one-room stone house, swept clean and neat: a simple woven mat, a low table with a white cloth and a round loaf of bread under a cover, a shelf with two clay jars. Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa straightens the cloth with a content smile while his daughter sweeps the doorstep. Soft afternoon light, wide interior view showing poverty and care. 3 Sunset glows orange through the small window. Chanina's daughter, standing on tiptoe, lights the small terracotta lamp on the shelf with a burning twig; the little flame dances and warm light spreads across the room. Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa watches from behind, smiling. Close-medium shot focused on her hands and the new flame. 4 In the lamplit room, Chanina's daughter stands by the shelf with drooping shoulders and teary, shining eyes. Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa kneels to her height, looking at her with concern and tenderness, one hand reaching out. The lamp burns softly behind them. Gentle warm light, close two-shot.
